themes: Exceptional execution across all segments despite Oswego fire temporary impact
Renewable energy expansion: 470 MW current, 414 MW additions in FY27 plan
Downstream premiumization and capacity additions: FRP, battery foil, AC fins ramping
Cost efficiency acceleration: $225M achieved toward $350-400M structural reduction goal
Captive coal mine development for margin enhancement and resource security
Safety and sustainability: zero fatalities, 80% waste recycled, 6.3M trees planted
risks: Novelis tariff impact persists: $70M this quarter from import dependence post-Oswego; recovery timeline uncertain
Copper market strain: negative TC/RC, tight concentrate supply expected through rest of year
Commodity and geopolitical volatility: aluminum prices volatile; Middle East conflict creates supply disruptions
High capex year for India expansion may constrain net debt improvement trajectory through FY27

analyst_pushback.question: Why did Novelis tariff impact jump $70M vs $24M prior quarter; should it be excluded from adjusted EBITDA?
analyst_pushback.response: Steve Fisher/Dev Ahuja: tariffs are real operational issue from Oswego downtime requiring imports; not adjustable; will persist near-term as supply chain normalizes

analyst_pushback.question: Downstream aluminum EBITDA per ton of $303 unsustainable; what is realistic run-rate?
analyst_pushback.response: Pai clarified: $250 sustainable for remaining FY27; long-term target over $300 driven by elevated MJP and product mix benefits

analyst_pushback.question: Novelis already at 4x leverage; how credible is below 4x target?
analyst_pushback.response: Dev Ahuja: both net debt reduction (insurance, working capital release) and EBITDA growth will drive improvement below 4x by year-end

analyst_pushback.question: Sambalpur smelter capex intensity appears steep vs other recent announcements in India.
analyst_pushback.response: Pai: trust actual project execution not announcements; our numbers calculated carefully; others are announcements only

tone_evidence: Confident on operational execution and long-term strategy; cautious on near-term tariffs and cost inflation; defensive on capex comparisons
